conservation.condition_narrative:
All paints appear secure and stable, despite microscopic, intermittent, limited, and superficial cracking in the paints at the right stretcher bar edge lip. There are also frame abrasions and retouching along all the top turn-down edge of the painting face, where the work historically rested against the rabbet of O'Keeffe's original frame. The paints in these edges are also stable and secure. The work is now moderately taut, and all keys have been taped in place to prevent them from falling and becoming wedged against the canvas verso in transit. The varnish is lightly soiled overall and particularly soiled at the top, bottom, and side margins from historic handling with soiled fingers and hands. This soiling appears superficial and may not permanently discolor the matte and porous paints applied by the artist. 
 
 
 
The stretcher lip creases along the viewer's left edge are an inherent result of aging. While this deterioration can become worse with time, it does not necessarily imply damage from handling and transport. The surface of the work exhibits a generalized, densely dispersed distribution of fine, sand-grain-appearing micro-protrusions. These are the result of alkaline pigment metal salts (2PbCO3·Pb(OH)2 and ZnO) in the priming and paints reacting with carboxylic acids and esters during periods of cycling humidity levels. The blister-like, thin-skinned grains are advanced in this work. The space between the glazing and painting in the front of the frame should be carefully examined for pinpoint and larger paint flakes that may have been dislodged by developing micro-protrusions.
conservation.technical_description:
**Support:** The support is a 1 x 1 twill-weave, processed linen canvas stretched over an "American Type" double-bevel-faced, miter-cut, mortise-and-tenon-joined, keyable softwood commercial stretcher bar, pre-cut to the whole inch, 1 ¾" wide x ¾" thick, in 20" and 16" lengths. The canvas is stretched with the warps in a horizontal position and tacked using blue steel tacks spaced evenly apart, 2" to 3" apart with regularity. The canvas has 44 warp threads per inch and 50 weft (twill weave) threads per inch. Eight custom basswood keys are secured at the corners. 
 
 
 
**Ground or Support Preparation:** The processed linen canvas has a commercially applied primer consisting of 2PbCO3•Pb(OH)2 and some CaCO3 in oil, characterized using x-ray fluorescence spectroscopy at 15kV, 33 and 40kV, and 28.8, 18, and 3.8 µA under full vacuum from the verso. 
 
  
 
**Design Layers:** The paints have been applied over charcoal/graphite line under-drawing in single layers, such that the texture of the primed canvas is visible through the paint, and the canvas or primer functions as a reflective surface. The artist has prepared her higher value whites and lighter colors so that they have a somewhat stiff, cream-like consistency, which is slightly thicker than background paints and holds brush texture as a compositional and textural effect. Darker values, by contrast, were prepared with more fluid, cream consistencies and allowed to flow and level into the texture of the canvas. O'Keeffe applies paint at the margins of forms using nearly continuous, curvilinear brush strokes with the brush positioned at a low angle to the canvas, resulting in a continuous, raised ridge of paint at the edge of each form. Surrounding brushwork is generally parallel to the linear directions defined by these edges, with no underlying or subsequent brushwork moving perpendicular to the linear form. Occasionally, adjacent forms do not overlap, and the artist has chosen to allow a "holiday" of unpainted, primed canvas to be a visible detail in the composition, with graphite underdrawing residues sometimes visible. The paints have been preliminarily characterized as iron red ochre, iron yellow ochre, lead white, and lead white and CaP bone black using X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy at 15kV and 33kV and 28.8 and 3.8 µA under full vacuum from three sample locations for each color. In this case, it is clear by the relative lack of micro-protrusions in the bone-black at the viewer's left margin that the Pb soap degradation is accelerated by the presence of basic Pb carbonate in the paints. 
 
 
 
**Surface Coating:** The painting has a thin, somewhat glossy synthetic acrylic varnish, apparently an iso-butyl methacrylate. 
 
  
 
**Framing, Backing, and Hanging Hardware:** The painting is installed in a reproduction Georgia O'Keeffe/George Of-designed "clam shell" profile, microenvironmental-controlled with Volara gasketing at the glazing and the backing, as well as silica gel-felted fabric in the backing panel, conditioned at 47% RH. The glazing is Optium, tin-optically coated, non-reflective acrylic.

titles.title: White Feather

credit_line: Gift of The Georgia O'Keeffe Foundation
description: The composition is a foreshortened vertical abstraction of a corner of an adobe fireplace with a white vase and feather sitting on the mantel adjacent to a yellow ochre vertical stripe. A single white feather has been placed in a white vase as the focal point of the work.
